title: Propagation Methods & Frequency Bands
markdown:
Electromagnetic waves travel from a transmitter to a receiver using one of three propagation methods, depending on the frequency band.

{{viz:0}}

---

### Propagation Methods

- **Ground Propagation** (below 2 MHz) — Waves follow the curvature of the Earth's surface. Used for long-range navigation and AM radio.
- **Sky Propagation** (2–30 MHz) — Waves are reflected off the ionosphere back to Earth, enabling long-distance communication beyond the horizon. Used for shortwave radio, CB radio, and maritime communication.
- **Line-of-Sight Propagation** (above 30 MHz) — Waves travel in a straight line from transmitter to receiver. Both antennas must be in direct view of each other. Used for FM radio, TV, cellular, satellite, and microwave links.

---

### Frequency Bands

The ITU divides the radio spectrum into eight named bands, each with characteristic propagation behavior and typical applications:

| Band | Range | Propagation | Application |
|---|---|---|---|
| VLF (very low frequency) | 3–30 kHz | Ground | Long-range radio navigation |
| LF (low frequency) | 30–300 kHz | Ground | Radio beacons and navigational locators |
| MF (medium frequency) | 300 kHz–3 MHz | Sky | AM radio |
| HF (high frequency) | 3–30 MHz | Sky | Citizens band (CB), ship/aircraft communication |
| VHF (very high frequency) | 30–300 MHz | Sky and line-of-sight | VHF TV, FM radio |
| UHF (ultrahigh frequency) | 300 MHz–3 GHz | Line-of-sight | UHF TV, cellular phones, paging, satellite |
| SHF (superhigh frequency) | 3–30 GHz | Line-of-sight | Satellite communication |
| EHF (extremely high frequency) | 30–300 GHz | Line-of-sight | Radar, satellite |

{{viz:1}}
